name: Design Intent vs Build Detail
title: Design Intent vs Build Detail
description: Design intent is what the designer meant - function, look, performance. Build detail is what the builder needs - dimensions, tolerances, sequences, tools. Translation makes intent buildable without changing what was meant.
how_it_works: Read the design asking 'what must be true for this to work' and write those as explicit requirements. Everything the builder must not guess gets written down; everything left unsaid is a future argument.
key_points: Intent: what the design must achieve.
Build detail: exactly how to achieve it.
Translation preserves intent while adding buildability.
Anything the builder must guess is a translation failure.
requirements: A source design artifact (sketch, CAD, description); stated build constraints (budget, tools, materials, timeline); a defined output format for the build instructions.
standards: ASME Y14 drawing standards for interpreting design intent; project documentation practice per company procedure.
citations: ASME Y14.5 dimensioning and tolerancing; standard mechanical drawing interpretation.
Design-for-manufacturing literature on translating intent into process (Boothroyd-Dewhurst DFM references).

title: Reading Engineering Drawings
